title: Tritium retention in plasma-facing walls
bottleneck: Plasma-facing materials trap tritium: co-deposited layers, implantation, and diffusion lock fuel into walls, especially in colder, inaccessible regions. Retained tritium is unavailable for burning, inflates the required plant inventory, and creates a distributed radioactive source that complicates maintenance and decommissioning. Lithium wall coatings, attractive for plasma performance, worsen retention dramatically. Recovering trapped tritium requires baking walls at high temperature or plasma-based desorption, both of which consume operating time and energy.
why_it_blocks: Every gram of tritium stuck in walls is a gram that must be bred, purchased, or accounted for. High retention can double the required tritium inventory and push the breeding ratio beyond what blankets can deliver.
current_state: Experiments at DIII-D quantified tritium trapping in lithium coatings, motivating heated-wall and tritium-removal techniques. Predictive models of retention over a plant lifetime remain uncertain.
